sources.title: Te Ahukaramū Charles Royal, Māori: Pre-European society, Te Ara
sources.note: Origins, The move inland, Traditional culture and Communal relationships. Arrival chronology is approximate; regional communities exercised distinct authority.

sources.title: Richard Walter and colleagues, Mass Migration and the Polynesian Settlement of New Zealand (2017)
sources.note: Wairau Bar section: revised early fourteenth-century chronology, argillite-working debris, fishing equipment and subsistence remains. Production for export is an interpretation.

sources.title: Rebecca Kinaston and colleagues, The First New Zealanders: Patterns of Diet and Mobility Revealed through Isotope Analysis (2013)
sources.note: Abstract, Introduction and Discussion: dietary and childhood-residence variation. The September 2013 correction adds Hallie Buckley to writing credits; it does not revise the isotope findings.

sources.title: Dilys Johns, Geoffrey Irwin and Yun Sung, An early sophisticated East Polynesian voyaging canoe discovered on New Zealand’s coast (2014)
sources.note: Hull description, turtle motif and Dating the Canoe: native mataī, structural ribs and stringer, repairs and caulking. About 1400 estimates the last voyage, not the tree’s growth or an exact construction year.

sources.title: University of Otago, Unexpected early kūmara cultivation discovered in Otago study
sources.note: Ian Barber’s account of the Antiquity study: Triangle Flat, Manawhenua ki Mohua, pits dated 1290 to 1385 and kūmara-like starch. Botanical identification retains the study’s qualification.

sources.title: Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga, Ōtuataua Stonefields, List 6055
sources.note: Overview, Historical Narrative and Physical Description: possible fifteenth- or sixteenth-century stonefields, garden soils, shell middens, occupation and continuing ancestral connections.

sources.title: Manatū Taonga, Ōtuataua Stonefields, NZHistory
sources.note: Site account distinguishes Māori gardening and habitation remains from nineteenth-century European drystone walls.

sources.title: Rebecca Kinaston and colleagues, Horticultural intensification and plant-based diets of eighteenth-century Waikato Māori (2026)
sources.note: Abstract, Introduction, Results and Discussion: gardens, Tamahere S14/487, diet and childhood evidence.

sources.title: Awhina Tamarapa, editor, Whatu Kākahu: Māori Cloaks, Te Papa Press (2011), sample chapters
sources.note: Printed pages 11, 53 and 76 to 77: muka, rain-cape construction, raranga and whatu. These describe craft traditions; no exact invention year is assigned.

sources.title: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, Origins of Māori Weaving
sources.note: Whakapapa, The Māori creation story and The domain of women: attributed tradition concerning Hine-te-iwaiwa and the transmission of weaving knowledge.

sources.title: Te Whare Taonga o Te Awamutu Museum, Uenuku: A Tainui Taonga
sources.note: Carving description and Tainui tradition. The museum’s broad traditional date is not a scientific production date or proof of national political unity.

sources.title: Paul Meredith, Matariki: Te Tau Hou Māori, Te Ara
sources.note: Story summary, What is Matariki? and The cycle of life and death: seasonal observation, remembrance and harvest sharing; practices differ among iwi.

sources.title: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, Pā kahawai, OL000106/10
sources.note: Item details and Overview: production 1750 to 1850, polished pāua shell, notches, shell barb and muka binding. The description of this particular lure takes precedence over the general account of wooden-shanked lures.

sources.title: Rongowhakaata and the Crown, Deed of Settlement, 30 September 2011
sources.note: Part 4, clauses 4.2 to 4.3 and 4.12 to 4.13: early 1840s construction of Te Hau ki Tūranga, forcible removal in 1867 and Crown acknowledgement and apology.

sources.title: Te Rua Mahara o te Kāwanatanga Archives New Zealand, What te Tiriti o Waitangi says in English and te reo Māori
sources.note: Comparison of Articles 1 and 2: kāwanatanga, sovereignty and tino rangatiratanga. The different texts and expectations are preserved rather than reduced to a single uncontested transfer.

sources.title: Manatū Taonga, Land confiscation law passed, NZHistory
sources.note: 3 December 1863 account: confiscation legislation and affected communities.

sources.title: Te Kōhanga Reo National Trust, Te Orokohanganga
sources.note: Opening history and 1982 timeline: Pukeatua, language immersion and whānau management.
